name: Primero
description: Primero is a 16th-century Italian vying/showdown game. Players receive four cards. The prime (one card of each suit) gives the game its name. Card values: 7=21, 6=18, A=16, 5=15, 4=14, 3=13, 2=12, pictures=10. Reconstructions by Mark Waks, Jeff Suzuki; Berni and Cardano described variants.

content.text: Primero is a 16th-century Italian vying/showdown game. Players receive four cards. The prime (one card of each suit) gives the game its name. Card values: 7=21, 6=18, A=16, 5=15, 4=14, 3=13, 2=12, pictures=10. Reconstructions by Mark Waks, Jeff Suzuki; Berni and Cardano described variants.
16th-century Italy. Popular across Europe. Prime = one of each suit. Card values appear in Scopa, Tressette.

The deal is counter-clockwise, starting with the dealer. Each player receives four cards. In the English reconstruction, two cards are dealt to each player, then a betting phase, then two more cards each; in the Spanish version the four cards may be dealt one by one. The deck is typically 40 cards (Italian or Spanish strip); the Roman version uses the full 52-card pack.
